To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genetic diversity of 127 strains of Xanthomonas pathogens of mango and pepper tree, which were isolated in 14 different tropical countries, was assessed by using restriction fragment length polymorphisms (RFLPs).
the Xanthomonads that cause mango bacterial black spot are genetically very similar to the Xanthomonad that causes bacterial leaf streak of rice and are genetically distinct from other Xanthomonads.
the Xanthomonads that cause mango bacterial black spot are genetically diverse and that strains isolated from mangoes in Southeast Asia, where the mango originated, are the most diverse.

understanding the genetic diversity of the Xanthomons pathovar mangiferaindicae.
the molecular characterization of Xanthomonas strains from mango, ambarella, pepper tree, and other plants.
the development and use of a rapid, sensitive, and reproducible method for the identification of Xanthomonas strains and the characterization of their genetic variability.

the genetic diversity of Xanthomonas mangiferae indicae is high and that the pathogen is a complex of strains that may be evolving separately.
Xanthomonas strains from pepper trees in the Mascarene islands are not Xanthomonas mangiferae-indicae.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Xanthomonas mangiferae-indicae strains have a relatively low degree of genetic variability and that there may be two groups of strains, one that is more closely related to strains of the X. oryze pv. oryze and the other that is more closely associated with strains from mango in Southeast Asia.

Xanthomonas strains isolated from mango in different geographic areas are genetically distinct, and the genetic diversity of Xanthomonas isolates from mango in Southeast Asia is greater than the genetic diversity of the other Xanthomonas groups.

there is a high degree of variability within the X. pv. mangifreaeindicae population, but that the variability can be grouped in ways that may be useful for the development of a disease management strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a great diversity among Xanthomonas strains that are pathogenic on mango, and the diversity is not limited to the host species.
the Xanthomonads causing mango bacterial black spot disease are not a single, uniform population but rather a diverse group of bacteria with a complex history of geographic spread and evolution.
the genetic diversity of Xanthomonas pathogens can be assessed with molecular markers and that the genetic diversity can be used to determine the geographic origin of strains.
